items.title: New Fed chair faces critical test at Jackson Hole as inflation fears mount
items.text: Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh faces intense pressure at the Jackson Hole symposium to provide clarity on interest rate paths as US national debt exceeds $40 trillion and bond market volatility spikes. Analysts warn that Warsh’s stated reluctance to provide traditional forward guidance on monetary policy could exacerbate instability in the $30 trillion US government debt market, which is currently struggling with investor fatigue.

items.title: Gold's Rally Has Two Engines: Washington's Debt Dilemma and a Central Bank Buying Spree
items.text: Gold prices have surged to $4,661.60 per ounce, driven by a record 289 tonnes of central bank purchases in Q2 2026 and a 'debasement trade' fueled by concerns over US fiscal health. The US Treasury's recent buyback program for long-dated bonds is being interpreted by market strategists as 'soft financial repression,' prompting investors to shift toward gold as a hedge against potential dollar volatility.

items.title: How To Navigate Global Volatility: The $40T Debt Milestone, Central Bank Signals, and Crypto Risk Dynamics
items.text: The US national debt crossing the $40 trillion threshold has forced a structural shift in bond markets, where rising term premia—rather than just rate expectations—are driving long-term yields higher. Treasury auctions are increasingly 'tailing,' indicating that price-insensitive foreign buyers are retreating, leaving the market dependent on price-sensitive private investors who demand higher real interest rates to absorb supply.

items.title: Canada tariffs, Bessent's buyback funding, Scott Kirby's plans for United and more in Morning Squawk - CNBC
items.text: The U.S. has imposed 50% tariffs on Canadian goods following failed trade negotiations, with Canada planning reciprocal measures, creating significant cross-border trade friction that threatens to exacerbate recent market volatility. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is considering utilizing a portion of the $950 billion Treasury General Account to bolster government bond buyback operations, a move intended to stabilize yields amid ongoing fiscal concerns.

items.title: Nvidia earnings face a frustrating reality - Yahoo Finance
items.text: Nvidia's upcoming earnings report faces a high-stakes environment where the stock has historically declined in six of the last eight quarters despite strong performance, highlighting a 'sell the news' dynamic. Analysts suggest the next major re-rating for the stock will depend less on traditional earnings beats and more on the company's emerging narrative as a leader in open-source AI models and agentic infrastructure.

items.title: Bessent could tap near $1 trillion Treasury General Account to fund bond buybacks, sources said
items.text: Treasury officials are considering utilizing the $950 billion Treasury General Account (TGA) to fund expanded bond buyback operations, potentially providing significant liquidity to stabilize long-term yields. The proposed strategy, dubbed a 'Treasury Twist,' would shift from relying solely on short-term bill issuance to using existing cash reserves, signaling a more aggressive interventionist stance by the Treasury.

items.title: This market shift resembles the post–World War II era — and bond yields could have room to go higher, says Morgan Stanley
items.text: Morgan Stanley analysts suggest the current economic environment mirrors the post-WWII era, characterized by structural deficits and fiscal pressures that may force long-term bond yields to remain elevated. The analysis implies that despite recent Treasury intervention attempts, the fundamental drivers of borrowing costs—specifically high capital expenditure and fiscal strain—could outweigh policy efforts to suppress yields.

items.title: China's First-Half Economic Performance Signals Stronger Momentum and Higher-Quality Growth
items.text: China reported a 4.7% GDP growth rate for the first half of 2026, supported by record-breaking trade figures exceeding 25 trillion yuan and a significant surge in high-value-added exports. The export sector is undergoing a structural shift, evidenced by a 188.8% increase in liquid cargo vessel exports and a 68.7% rise in electric vehicle shipments, highlighting China's growing competitiveness in high-end manufacturing.

items.title: US holds pace, euro area gains as China growth slows in Q2: Report
items.text: The Bundesbank suggests that China's underlying economic dynamics may be stronger than headline GDP figures indicate, as the country's export boom continues to drive industrial output despite broader global slowdowns. Global industrial production remains sensitive to geopolitical risks in the Middle East, with elevated energy costs and supply chain volatility posing ongoing inflationary pressures for major economies trading with China.

items.title: Six Leading Enterprises Jointly Awarded Tender for Hung Shui Kiu/Ha Tsuen Pilot Development Area
items.text: A consortium including China Overseas Land & Investment, JD.com, and Sino Land has secured the tender for the Hung Shui Kiu/Ha Tsuen pilot area with a total planned investment of HK$16.8 billion. The project aims to develop a smart logistics hub integrated with residential and commercial facilities, serving as a strategic pillar for the Northern Metropolis and enhancing Greater Bay Area connectivity.

items.title: Hong Kong homebuyers snap up units at The Sterling as value-focused demand deepens
items.text: China Resources Land’s 'The Sterling' project generated HK$1.6 billion in sales, with 46,000 subscriptions setting a record for first-round interest in a local residential development. The project's success, priced 27% to 33% below 2021 market levels, signals that buyer demand remains highly sensitive to competitive pricing and urban connectivity rather than a broad market recovery.

items.title: Big Tech’s Teacher AI Program Costs $23 Million. Microsoft Spends That Every 74 Minutes
items.text: Major tech firms are utilizing education partnerships as a low-cost demand-generation strategy, with the $23 million National Academy for AI Instruction representing only 74 minutes of Microsoft's quarterly capital expenditure. By funding nonprofits that lobby for mandatory computer science credits, tech companies are effectively embedding their proprietary AI tools into state-mandated curricula, creating a captive market for their software.

items.title: Trump Bought SpaceX, Palantir And More: What We Learned From Latest Stock Trades
items.text: Ethics filings reveal over 1,000 stock trades in June, including significant activity in defense and tech firms like Palantir and SpaceX that maintain substantial government contracts. The high volume of trading, which reached an estimated 14,000 transactions in 2025, continues to draw scrutiny from lawmakers regarding the transparency and potential conflicts of interest within the presidential blind trust.

items.title: Hugging Face Considers $13 Billion Sale of Its AI Platform
items.text: The AI developer platform is exploring a potential sale at a $13 billion valuation, a significant jump from its $4.5 billion valuation during its 2023 Series D funding round. The move highlights investor appetite for infrastructure-layer AI companies that facilitate model development, following similar high-value acquisitions like Stripe's purchase of OpenRouter for approximately $8 billion.

items.title: Alibaba issues €8.7 billion in new shares to finance Artificial Intelligence (AI)
items.text: Alibaba is raising €8.7 billion through a new share issuance specifically earmarked to accelerate its artificial intelligence capabilities and infrastructure. This massive capital injection signals a major strategic pivot toward AI-driven growth, likely aimed at maintaining competitiveness against domestic and international cloud and AI rivals.

items.title: Nvidia raising AI server prices more than 15% amid memory costs
items.text: Nvidia is implementing a price hike of over 15% on its AI servers, a move primarily driven by the rising costs of high-bandwidth memory components. This pricing strategy suggests that Nvidia maintains significant pricing power in the AI hardware market, allowing it to pass supply chain cost pressures directly to its Big Tech customers.

items.title: Taiwan Reportedly Indicted NVIDIA Employees For Exporting Prohibited AI Servers To China
items.text: Taiwanese authorities have indicted Nvidia employees for their alleged involvement in smuggling restricted AI server technology into China, violating strict export control regulations. This legal development highlights ongoing geopolitical risks and compliance challenges for Nvidia as it navigates U.S. and international trade restrictions on advanced semiconductor exports.

items.title: Europe’s EV Sales Explode, Now Making Up A Quarter Of New Cars
items.text: European EV sales surged 51% in July, capturing a 25% market share as rising fuel prices drive consumer adoption across the EU, UK, and Switzerland. While Tesla models lead in year-to-date registrations, the Skoda Elroq emerged as the top-selling EV in July, signaling increased competition from legacy European manufacturers.

items.title: Chinese EV market booms south of US border in Mexico
items.text: Electrified vehicle sales in Mexico grew 44% in the first half of 2026, with Chinese manufacturers capturing approximately 70% of the local EV market share. The disparity between Mexican availability and U.S. import tariffs has created a unique cross-border arbitrage, where dual-citizens are purchasing cheaper Chinese EVs in Mexico for personal use.

items.title: AI Data Center Boom Faces Growing Regulatory and Social Backlash
items.text: The rapid expansion of AI infrastructure has hit a structural wall, with at least 75 projects worth approximately US$130 billion delayed or blocked in Q1 2026 due to local opposition and resource concerns. State-level legislative risks are escalating, as New York and over a dozen other states consider temporary construction bans to mitigate the strain on local energy and water grids.

items.title: NVIDIA Expands AI Infrastructure Ecosystem with Poolside and Cloverleaf Deals
items.text: NVIDIA is deepening its full-stack AI strategy through a US$7 billion investment and licensing deal with Poolside AI, aiming to control more of the model-building workflow and increase customer lock-in. The partnership with Cloverleaf Infrastructure signals a strategic move to secure AI-ready power and land sites, directly addressing the primary bottleneck currently hindering large-scale data center deployment.

items.title: Space launch stocks fall despite Trump's push for 1,000 annual launches
items.text: Despite a federal mandate aiming for 1,000 annual launches by 2030—a massive increase from last year's 178—major space stocks like SpaceX, Rocket Lab, and AST SpaceMobile have experienced downward pressure. Market participants are prioritizing near-term execution risks and operational milestones, such as Rocket Lab’s critical Neutron test launch, over the long-term potential of government-backed policy shifts.

items.title: India Puts Its First Private Rocket Into Orbit As Europe Still Waits for Its Own
items.text: Skyroot Aerospace has become the first Indian private company to reach orbit, signaling a successful transition from state-dominated space programs to a commercialized ecosystem supported by government policy. India aims to scale its space economy from $8.4 billion in 2022 to $44 billion by 2033, leveraging private sector innovation to capture a larger share of the global small-satellite launch market.

items.title: Kids outlearn AI—and we still don’t know why
items.text: Current LLMs require roughly 100,000 times more data to achieve linguistic fluency than a human child, highlighting a massive inefficiency in current AI scaling paradigms. With frontier models now training on trillions of tokens, the industry faces a looming 'data wall' where high-quality, easily available human-generated data may be exhausted as early as the 2030s. The reliance on massive datasets for model performance is becoming a strategic bottleneck, forcing researchers to pivot toward reverse-engineering human cognitive development to achieve better results with less data. Closing the data efficiency gap is now a critical objective for AI architects, as future model improvements will likely depend on architectural innovation rather than simply increasing the volume of training data.

items.title: The Download: kids outlearning AI, and space travel agents
items.text: A significant political shift is emerging as both US political parties increasingly oppose AI data centers ahead of the midterms, citing environmental and infrastructure concerns. New Amazon data center projects are facing scrutiny for their potential to become some of the most polluting power plants in the United States. The luxury travel market is expanding into the orbital sector, with firms like SpaceVIP positioning themselves as intermediaries for private citizens seeking multi-million dollar missions to the International Space Station. Cognitive scientists are investigating the 'data efficiency gap' to understand how children master language with significantly less input than LLMs, which may hold the key to future breakthroughs in AI training efficiency.

items.title: Xiaomi unveils 3-nm Xring D100 smart-driving chip, plans commercial use in 2027
items.text: Xiaomi has unveiled the Xring D100, China's first 3-nm high-computing-power smart-driving chip, capable of running 200-billion-parameter models locally. The chip has completed validation and is slated for commercial deployment in 2027, marking a significant step in Xiaomi's vertical integration strategy. Xiaomi has invested over 21 billion yuan in its chip development program, employing nearly 3,000 experts to reduce reliance on external suppliers like Nvidia.

items.title: Leapmotor stays profitable in H1 as margin and cash flow weaken
items.text: Leapmotor achieved its second consecutive half-year of profitability with a net profit of 210 million yuan, representing a 600% year-on-year increase. Despite revenue growth of 57.2%, the company's gross margin narrowed to 11.7% due to rising raw material costs and shifts in product mix. Free cash flow plummeted 83.7% to 140 million yuan, reflecting increased procurement spending and inventory stocking. Overseas expansion is a critical growth engine, with exports surging 372.6% to account for 27% of total sales in the first half of 2026.

items.title: Multi-Die Assemblies Dominate At 2nm And Below
items.text: Heterogeneous integration and multi-die assemblies have become essential for leading-edge servers and edge devices as traditional monolithic scaling hits physical and economic limits. The shift is driven by the inability to pack sufficient compute power into a single reticle-sized die, necessitating a move toward chiplets to meet the performance demands of data-heavy AI workloads. Agentic AI is further complicating design requirements by demanding a mix of CPUs, GPUs, and specialized accelerators, requiring AI-driven validation tools to ensure manufacturability and testability. Industry leaders are targeting two orders of magnitude improvements in performance-per-watt, a goal that requires a fundamental realignment of manufacturing processes, advanced packaging, and logic scaling.

items.title: NousResearch/hermes-agent
items.text: Built on a modular Python architecture designed for long-term agentic memory and task persistence. Focuses on self-improving workflows that evolve based on user interaction patterns. A highly adaptive, scalable AI agent framework designed for continuous learning and growth.

items.text: Written in Rust for high-performance, local-first data processing and memory management. Acts as a central orchestrator for multi-agent systems, enabling complex workflow delegation. A local-first personal AI orchestrator that manages agent fleets and builds a private memory of your life.

items.text: Curated educational resource covering hardware architecture, memory bandwidth, and kernel optimization. Includes practical methodologies for profiling and bottleneck analysis in GPU-accelerated environments. A comprehensive curriculum for mastering GPU performance engineering, mirroring techniques used by frontier AI labs.

A terminal-based interface providing free access to advanced coding models like Claude Code and Codex.

items.text: Python-based pipeline that parses technical literature into structured agent-ready knowledge. Allows developers to 'teach' their AI agents specific proprietary or niche technical domains. Enhances agentic performance by providing domain-specific context for coding and debugging tasks. Streamlines the process of keeping AI assistants updated with the latest technical documentation. A tool that converts technical PDF documentation and books into actionable skills for Claude Code.

items.title: Stock Market Today (Aug. 24, 2026): Nasdaq slides on Iran sanctions, U.S.-Canada tariff threats - Yahoo Finance
items.text: Markets are bracing for significant volatility as investors await Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's announcement of new financial sanctions against Iran, which are being framed as a major financial offensive. The upcoming Federal Reserve symposium in Jackson Hole, specifically a keynote speech by Kevin Warsh, is a critical focal point for investors seeking clarity on the Fed's long-term inflation philosophy and potential policy shifts.

items.title: Nvidia is paying $6 billion to license AI model software from startup Poolside
items.text: Nvidia has committed $6 billion to license AI model software from the startup Poolside, signaling an aggressive expansion into the software-as-a-service layer of the AI ecosystem. This massive capital allocation suggests Nvidia is moving beyond hardware dominance to capture more value from the software stack, potentially creating new recurring revenue streams for the company.

items.text: Built on Claude Code for local execution and privacy. Automates the end-to-end job search pipeline including CV tailoring and cover letter generation. Designed for personal ownership, allowing users to fork and customize their own job-hunting agent. Provides structured evaluation of job postings to filter for high-probability matches. An autonomous AI job application framework that runs locally to evaluate postings, tailor CVs, and prepare for interviews.

items.text: Essential infrastructure resource for bootstrapping fintech and startup projects. Categorized by service type including cloud hosting, databases, and monitoring tools. Helps developers minimize operational costs during the early stages of product development. Regularly updated to reflect current market offerings and tier changes. A comprehensive, community-maintained list of SaaS, PaaS, and IaaS offerings with free tiers for developers.

items.title: Dan Ives Says Investors Still Underestimate Nvidia Days Before Earnings
items.text: Analyst Dan Ives contends that current market models for Nvidia are 15% to 20% too low, arguing that Wall Street fails to fully account for the scale of physical AI and hyperscaler demand. Key metrics to watch in the upcoming earnings include Q3 guidance, confirmation of Vera Rubin shipments, and visibility into $1 trillion in Blackwell-related revenue through 2027.

items.title: GE Vernova Launches Medium-Voltage Power System for AI Data Centers
items.text: GE Vernova is shifting power protection to the medium-voltage level to address the extreme power density and volatility requirements of modern AI data centers. The new MV-UPS system, scheduled for commercial shipment in mid-2027, aims to simplify downstream electrical infrastructure and assist operators in meeting increasingly stringent grid-connection and power-quality compliance standards.

items.text: Implements a 'lazy' heuristic to prioritize existing solutions and minimal code footprint. Designed to integrate into developer workflows to reduce technical debt and bloat. Utilizes LLM reasoning to evaluate whether a feature is necessary before implementation. Useful for rapid prototyping and maintaining clean, maintainable codebases. An AI agent framework optimized for minimalist, high-efficiency code generation.

items.title: Global Markets Brace for Inflation, AI and Policy Signals
items.text: Global energy markets face significant volatility due to disruptions near the Strait of Hormuz, complicating the inflation outlook and challenging the ability of central banks to maintain a disinflationary path. Investors are closely monitoring the upcoming central bank summit in Wyoming, seeking clarity on whether policymakers will maintain restrictive interest rates or pivot to support economic growth amid rising fiscal concerns.

items.title: Uzbekistan Pushes for a More Connected and Competitive Central Asia
items.text: Uzbekistan reported strong economic momentum with 8.5% GDP growth in H1 2026 and $8.3 billion in foreign investment in Q1, signaling a successful transition toward deeper market integration. The government is aggressively pursuing investment-grade credit ratings and has set a target of $1 billion in fintech investment by 2030, supported by new regulatory frameworks for digital payments and open banking.

items.title: Central bank likely intervenes in forex market, anchoring rupee amid global turmoil: Traders
items.text: The Reserve Bank of India is actively utilizing state-run banks to offer dollars, effectively anchoring the rupee at 95.64 against the dollar to mitigate volatility from the US-Iran conflict. Robust balance of payments inflows have provided the RBI with the necessary liquidity to defend the currency, providing a stabilizing influence for investors exposed to Indian market assets.

items.title: A massive trade just happened in gold. The options market is buzzing
items.text: A trader executed a massive bearish bet on the SPDR Gold Shares ETF (GLD) by selling 116,000 in-the-money 420-strike calls and purchasing 430-strike calls, creating a net credit of $58 million. The trade establishes a breakeven point at $425, signaling an expectation for a short-term pullback in gold prices despite the asset's 15% rally this month and broader bullish options sentiment.

items.title: Trump is threatening new Canadian auto tariffs. That will hurt US automakers and workers
items.text: President Trump has threatened a 50% tariff on all Canadian auto imports, a move that could disrupt the highly integrated North American supply chain where parts and vehicles cross borders multiple times. Analysts warn that such tariffs would act as a 'body blow' to the industry, potentially forcing plant closures and job losses in the US, as Canadian-built vehicles rely heavily on American-made components.

items.title: Prediction market traders doubtful Bessent’s bond interventions will push yields lower
items.text: Traders on prediction platforms like Kalshi and Polymarket are signaling skepticism toward Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent’s efforts to cap yields, with a 56% probability assigned to the 10-year Treasury yield remaining at or above 4.75% through year-end. Despite the Treasury's plan to double debt buybacks and potential utilization of the $1 trillion General Account, market participants view these interventions as temporary measures that fail to address the underlying structural pressures of a $40 trillion national debt.

items.title: Goldman Sachs Warns China's Q3 Growth Could Fall Below 4.5% Target; Easing Expectations Surge
items.text: Goldman Sachs estimates Q3 GDP growth has decelerated to approximately 4% year-over-year, falling below Beijing's official 4.5% to 5% target range due to persistent demand-side weakness. The deterioration in July data has triggered a surge in market expectations for imminent monetary easing, with analysts warning that structural damage may occur without stronger fiscal intervention.

items.title: Heavyweights give Northern Metropolis vote of confidence with HK$1.03b land win
items.text: A six-company consortium, including JD.com and major developers like Sino Land and China Resources Land, secured a 10.5-hectare site in Hung Shui Kiu with a HK$1.03 billion bid. The project involves a total investment of HK$16.8 billion and requires the development of an intelligent logistics center, signaling a strategic push to integrate e-commerce infrastructure into the Northern Metropolis.

items.title: How to choose between Big Tech or startups
items.text: Big Tech firms including Amazon and Meta have collectively shed over 27,000 jobs in the past year, signaling a shift away from the historical perception of these giants as stable, low-risk employers. Despite ongoing workforce reductions, large tech companies continue to attract talent through superior compensation packages and the unique opportunity for engineers to work on large-scale systems impacting billions of users.

items.title: Which countries, tech giants around the world are regulating kids' social media access?
items.text: Global regulatory pressure is intensifying, with Australia imposing fines of up to 49.5 million Australian dollars for non-compliance with under-16 social media bans, creating significant operational and legal risks for platforms like Meta and TikTok. Governments in Britain and beyond are pushing for device-level technical mandates that would force companies like Apple and Google to integrate content-blocking software, potentially altering core product architecture and user experience.

items.title: Prediction: Not Micron. This Artificial Intelligence (AI) Stock Could Be the Biggest Winner of the Next Infrastructure Bottleneck
items.text: The optical networking market is projected to surge from $15 billion this year to $154 billion by 2028, driven by the critical need for high-speed connectivity within AI data center clusters. Marvell Technology is positioned as a primary beneficiary of this infrastructure shift, reportedly controlling 60% to 65% of the digital signal processor market essential for data center interconnects.

items.title: Prediction: This Artificial Intelligence (AI) Stock Will Go Parabolic After Nvidia Reports Earnings on Aug. 26
items.text: Major hyperscalers including Microsoft, Amazon, and Alphabet have committed to a combined annual capital expenditure exceeding $700 billion, signaling sustained demand for AI-related compute infrastructure. Nvidia's upcoming earnings report is expected to show 97% year-over-year revenue growth, with analysts highlighting a $2.3 trillion backlog among cloud providers as a key indicator of continued pricing power.

items.title: Nvidia says Groq racks will be online this year following $20 billion purchase
items.text: Nvidia has moved its Groq 3 LPX inference racks into full production, utilizing 500 megabytes of on-die SRAM to minimize memory bottlenecks and deliver 3,400 tokens per second. The commercialization of this $20 billion acquisition targets premium, latency-sensitive AI agent workloads, allowing cloud providers to offer tiered service agreements for complex, multistep tasks.

items.title: Memory Stocks Slide on Report Apple May Source Chinese Chips: SanDisk Down 9%, Micron and Western Digital Down 7%
items.text: Memory sector stocks experienced a sharp sell-off following reports that the U.S. government may allow Apple to source DRAM and NAND flash from Chinese suppliers CXMT and YMTC. While analysts suggest the market reaction may be an overreaction due to technical qualification hurdles for Chinese suppliers, the news highlights significant geopolitical risk for U.S. and Korean memory manufacturers.

items.title: Tesla Maintained Its Majority of the U.S. EV Market in Q2, but That's Not All You Need to Know
items.text: Tesla maintained a 50.5% share of the U.S. EV market in Q2 2026, though this majority is largely a result of domestic competitors experiencing sharper sales declines than Tesla's 13% drop. While global deliveries rose 25% year-over-year to 480,126 units, the company is steadily losing market share in China and Europe to aggressive local competitors like BYD and Volkswagen.

items.title: Trump’s Iran war supercharged EV sales everywhere except the U.S.
items.text: Geopolitical instability in the Middle East has driven oil prices above $100 per barrel, creating a significant macro-economic tailwind for EV adoption in Europe, Southeast Asia, and Latin America. The removal of U.S. federal tax credits has caused a divergence in market performance, as global EV sales surged following the energy crisis while the U.S. market faced a 20% decline in Q2.

items.title: Data Center Construction at Midyear: Demand, Friction, and Building Discipline
items.text: Zurich’s specialized Data Center Project Guard insurance offering has received broker submissions representing approximately $140 billion in project value since January, signaling massive capital-intensive demand. Regulatory friction is mounting as states like New York implement construction pauses and Texas initiates audits, forcing developers to navigate increasing community concerns over energy, water, and grid stability.

items.title: Prometheus’ 1.5 GW Texas Data Center Plan Tests Private Power
items.text: Prometheus Hyperscale is bypassing the ERCOT grid by planning a 1.5 GW 'islanded' campus in West Texas, utilizing onsite natural gas generation to avoid interconnection delays. The project requires significant operational complexity, including managing firm fuel supplies and redundancy, and remains contingent on securing a customer commitment for a 2027 delivery target.

items.title: White House Policy Sets Goal of Supporting 1,000 Rocket Launches a Year by 2030
items.text: The new National Space Transportation Policy mandates that the Pentagon and federal agencies develop infrastructure to support 1,000 annual launches by 2030, representing a fivefold increase from 2025 levels. Agencies must submit findings by February regarding necessary resources and authorities to expand launch capacity, as current facilities at Vandenberg and Cape Canaveral are nearing their operational limits.

items.title: Goodbye, Falcon 9: SpaceX planning to retire workhorse launcher when Starship is up and running
items.text: Elon Musk confirmed plans to phase out the Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy rockets in favor of the fully reusable Starship, which is designed to achieve a launch cadence of several times per day. The transition will shift production resources toward Starship, forcing commercial operators to migrate to the new platform as SpaceX potentially discontinues most Falcon 9 missions by 2028.

items.title: Xpeng to launch G9L in September, Mona L05 in Q4 as it targets 60,000 monthly sales
items.text: Xpeng aims to reach 60,000 monthly vehicle deliveries in Q4 2026, representing a 58% increase over July's performance. The company is launching the G9L flagship SUV in September and the Mona L05 in Q4 to expand its coverage across major SUV segments. Production of the Mona L03 has shifted to a double-shift schedule to address supply-chain bottlenecks and meet growing demand. The G9L features an 800-volt charging platform and offers both BEV and EREV variants, directly targeting competitors like Li Auto and Aito.
